result:
I graded submission s1 for quiz 0001 and wrote the grades to `grades/0001-s1.json`: 2 correct, 2 partial and 2 wrong.

| Item | Verdict | Feedback |
|---|---|---|
| q1 | correct | An agent is a loop of choose an action, run it, get the result back. |
| q2 | wrong (M4) | The model outputs a tool request. It does not open the booking system itself. |
| q3 | correct | A step limit is the safeguard, because more steps add nothing when the agent repeats itself. |
| q4 | wrong (M4) | The answer is 4 model calls, not 1: three tool requests plus the final answer. The program runs the tools. |
| q5 | partial | "It sends it back to the model" is right. It is missing why: so the model can pick its next step or write the final answer. |
| q6 | partial (M3) | Choosing a tool from its description is right. The claim that the model remembers earlier sessions on its own is wrong. |

**Summary:** You have the shape of the loop down. The one idea to fix is that the model only writes text, and the program does everything else: it runs the tools, feeds results back, calls the model again and supplies any memory. That idea is behind both the q2 and q4 misses and the extra claim in q6.

I also added a learning record, `learning-records/0003-model-writes-program-acts.md`, and updated `NOTES.md`. s2 is still ungraded.

**Next step:** Redraw your laser-cutter trace in two columns, "model writes" and "program does", and count the model calls. Then bring it to the context and memory session.

Do you want me to grade s2 next, to see whether the model/program split stuck after four days?
